summary: The root وعي primarily means to understand, comprehend, or retain knowledge. It implies being aware and mindful, often in the context of remembering or preserving something in one's mind.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: He kept it in mind, and considered it. (Msb.) وَعَى الحَدِيثَ He kept, or retained, the narration in his mind, or memory; or knew it, or learned it, by heart; and studied it until he knew it. (Msb.) وَعَى, aor. وَعِىَ, He heeded; paid attention to.
أَوْعَاهُ الحَدِيثَ He made him to retain the narration in his memory; or to know it, or learn it, by heart. (TA, in art. زكت.)

A [ bag, or wallet, or] receptacle, for travelling-provisions, and for goods or utensils, &c.: (S, MA:) a vessel (?). وِعَآءُ القَلْبِ [ The pericardium ]. (TA, voce فُؤَادٌ.) بَتَثْتُ لَهُ مَا فِى وِعَائِى (assumed tropical:) I showed him what was in my heart. (Er-Rághib, TA, in art. شكو and شكى.) حَرْفُ الوِعَآءِ [ The adverbial particle فِى ]. (IB, in TA, art. وسط.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
